definitions.explanation: An X-ray image or X-ray examination. Named after Wilhelm Röntgen, the discoverer of X-rays. Used in everyday Japanese to refer to both the procedure and the resulting image.

examples.japanese: レントゲン⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{撮|と}る→撮る：00760_toru⟧。
レントゲン⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{骨折|こっせつ}→骨折：02763_kossetsu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{見|み}つかった→見つかる：01173_mitsukaru⟧。
examples.english: A fracture was found on the X-ray.

examples.japanese: ⟦{健康|けんこう}{診断|しんだん}→健康診断：05979_kenkoushindan⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{胸|むね}→胸：00972_mune⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧レントゲン⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{撮|と}って→撮る：00760_toru⟧⟦もらった→もらう：00520_morau⟧。
examples.english: I had a chest X-ray taken during my health checkup.

notes:
レントゲン is the standard everyday word for X-ray in Japanese, named after Wilhelm Röntgen. The more technical term is エックス⟦{線|せん}→線：09901_sen⟧ (X-ray).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- レントゲン⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{撮|と}る→撮る：00760_toru⟧: to take an X-ray
- レントゲン{写真|しゃしん}: X-ray photograph
- レントゲン⟦{検査|けんさ}→検査：02707_kensa⟧: X-ray examination
- ⟦{胸|むね}→胸：00972_mune⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧レントゲン: chest X-ray

USAGE:
In everyday conversation, レントゲン is far more common than エックス⟦{線|せん}→線：09901_sen⟧. It is used by both patients and medical staff in casual settings, while エックス⟦{線|せん}→線：09901_sen⟧ appears in formal medical documentation.
